operational_risks: Sentinel was blind for about 61 hours, from 2026-09-17 10:07 UTC to 2026-09-19 23:19 UTC. The shared Anthropic prepaid credit hit zero and every Haiku call failed with HTTP 400 'credit balance too low' (689 classification and 329 vagueness-check errors in the journal). No article was classified in that window, so no urgency 9-10 alert could have fired. Service came back only when the owner bought $20 by hand at 23:16 UTC.

Root cause: auto-reload failed and Anthropic paused it on Aug 18, and again on Sep 13 when the card was declined for insufficient funds. After Sep 13 nothing refilled the balance. The 'credit balance is low' warning ($2.19, Sep 15) and the 'API access is turned off' email (Sep 17) both reached the owner's mailbox and were later trashed by the 2026-10-01/02 mail cleanup. No spend notification is configured in the Console today. A $100 monthly API-spend threshold notice did exist and fired on 2026-05-27, so that setting was later removed or replaced by the $150 org spend limit. Either way it warned about spending, not about a low balance.

Shared balance: other projects draw on the same prepaid pool. On May 20-21 the MemSearch backfill burned $86.47 in about 16 hours and would have emptied the balance if the $150 had not been bought. A burst from any other key can starve Sentinel whenever Sentinel runs on Anthropic.

Rollback exposure today: Sentinel does not currently depend on Anthropic. But the legacy Haiku path is still wired and is also the code default in sentinel/config.py, and the Sentinel key is still active. A rollback would start on a shared $18.77 balance, about 5.6 days at today's volume (~$3.38/day at Haiku list price). It would then rely on auto-reload (below $10, top up to $20) with the same card that declined twice. The org spend limit of $150/month covers the central rollback estimate (~$103/month) and the busiest October week (~$118/month) plus msigalert. It does not cover the high bound with the tokenizer allowance (~$153/month); in that case Sentinel classification would stop late in the month when the limit is hit.

Mail-cleanup risk: the 2026-10-02 cleanup trashed at least 19 Anthropic billing emails, including the low-balance and access-off warnings. Future warnings may vanish the same way before the owner sees them. Since Sep 19 the billing entity is Anthropic Ireland, which sends from a different Stripe sender, so any mail filter keyed on the old sender will miss its receipts and failure notices.

Credit expiry: the remaining $18.77 expires about 2027-09-20. At msigalert's ~$0.52/month, roughly $12-13 would expire unused. This is a minor cash leak, not a Sentinel cost unless Sentinel uses the credit.
open_questions: Owner decision: the Sep 19 $20 purchase was the manual fix for Sentinel's outage. Should the cash view attribute the whole $20 to Sentinel because it triggered the purchase? The default here is FIFO consumption share: $0.88 of it consumed by Sentinel, and $18.76 still unconsumed.

Invoice numbers 0006-0008 and 0010 are missing from the Console list. They fit exactly the three failed May 20 attempts and the failed Aug 18 auto-reload, which were probably voided. The Sep 13 failed auto-reload also left no listed invoice. The balance reconciles to within $0.02, which rules out any material hidden paid credit. The owner may confirm, but it is low priority.

Billing settings history: the Console now reads 'below $10, top up to $20', but the Aug 19 and Sep 1 recharges were about $10 each, made when the balance was about $4-6. That fits a different setting at the time. Was it changed after the outage? Should auto-reload stay on now that only msigalert uses the org? Also, a $100 monthly spend-threshold notification existed on 2026-05-27, and none is set today: was it removed on purpose?
Should the still-active Project Sentinel API key be revoked, or kept deliberately for a Haiku rollback? If kept, add a Console spend notification and a balance check to Sentinel's health monitoring.

result.method_notes:
- **Monthly Sentinel cost.** Each amount is the usage of the Anthropic Console's 'Project Sentinel' API key. The figures come from Console cost and usage pages filtered by key, and the March-September 2026 token exports priced at the Haiku 4.5 list price of $1 input / $5 output per MTok.
  - The key has no caching, discounts or other models.
  - Token-exact amounts are used for full precision. Each one equals the Console's displayed monthly total to the cent: 1.56, 8.41, 18.87, 19.89, 21.96, 21.67 and 16.51. October is 0.
  - Sentinel's total is 108.886254 USD; the displayed monthly totals sum to 108.87.
  - The org total is 197.110900 = Sentinel 108.886254 + MemSearchBacklog 86.47 + msigalert 1.754646. It matches the Console's $197.11 to the cent. It is not token-exact, because the MemSearch figure is UI-derived from cent-rounded totals.
  - Raw CSV row sums (197.36) were not used, because the rows are rounded to cents.
- **What the key covers.** It covers everything Sentinel sent to Anthropic: production classification, the unstored vagueness-check calls (May 22-Sep 20), retries, local dev (March) and the May calibration evals.
  - That is why the provider figures run about 20% above the previous audit's DB-token estimates, which totalled 101.35.
  - The September 'residual' of $2.08 is Sentinel's own vagueness-check calls.
- **Excluded usage on the same org.** The MemSearchBacklog key (Sonnet 4.6, May 20-21) and the msigalert keys (Sonnet 5 and Opus 5) are excluded.
  - No key-less Console or Workbench usage and no Claude Code API usage exists.
  - Haiku calls routed through OpenRouter during the Sep 20-24 evals ($2.668698, 586 requests) are billed by OpenRouter and belong to that group, not to these lines.
- **Cash and VAT.** There are five paid credit grants, all reverse charge at 0% VAT, so no VAT is included.
  - Mar 21: $25 (Link). May 20: $150 (Link). Aug 19: $10.86 auto-recharge (card). Sep 1: $10.00 auto-recharge (card). Sep 19: $20 (card, Anthropic Ireland).
  - Credits granted total 215.863756 against 215.86 cash paid.
  - cash_events.date is the provider receipt and invoice date (UTC). Where the Warsaw calendar date differs (May 20 purchase = May 21 01:15 Warsaw; Sep 19 purchase = Sep 20 01:16 Warsaw), the notes give it. For the $150 the preceding NBP business day is May 19 on the receipt date and May 20 on the Warsaw date; this result keeps the receipt date. The owner's bank statement date governs if the owner prefers it.
- **FIFO allocation.** Grants were assumed to be consumed oldest first (their expiries are also in purchase order).
  - The simulation is hour by hour. It uses daily cost rows scaled to the token-exact monthly totals, and exact daily tokens for September. It uses known times: grant receipt times, the MemSearch window from May 20 20:58 UTC to May 21 ~12:53 UTC, the outage hours, and an even spread within each day otherwise.
  - Results by grant:
    - Mar 21 grant: Sentinel 16.80, MemSearch 8.20.
    - May 20 grant: MemSearch 78.27, Sentinel 71.12, msigalert 0.60.
    - Aug 19 grant: Sentinel 10.17, msigalert 0.69.
    - Sep 1 grant: Sentinel 9.90, msigalert 0.10.
    - Sep 19 grant: Sentinel 0.88, msigalert 0.36, with 18.76 unconsumed.
  - Sentinel's cash shares sum to 108.879, against 108.886 economic. The difference is the small gap between credit units and cents charged, plus a $0.0034 simulated overdraft on Sep 17.
  - The simulation independently reproduces three provider facts: the $2.19 low-balance email (Sep 15 10:29 UTC), credit exhaustion at about 10:00 UTC on Sep 17 (email at 10:05, journal at 10:07), and the final balance of 18.756 against the Console's 18.77.
  - Script: [private audit workspace] scripts_anth/fifo.py
- **Corrections to earlier inputs.**
  - The email agent's claim that no API receipts exist was a deletion artifact; the receipts were trashed on 2026-10-02.
  - The deleted-mail inventory mislabelled the Sep 19 receipt as a Max subscription; the portal invoice shows a one-time API credit purchase.
  - The checker's figure of 1.75 is used for msigalert, not the portal agent's 1.77.
  - Sentinel is 108.89, not 108.87.
- **Free credit.** No free or promotional credit was consumed in 2026. No accrued unpaid charges exist, because the account is prepaid.
- **No conversion.** Amounts are in USD, unconverted.
- **Resolver decisions (verifier 1, numbers).** Every booked line, cash event and balance was confirmed; no booked amount changed.

Scope: OpenRouter and TypeSafe (Jev). Both are shared prepaid accounts. Sentinel used them only for offline evaluations in September 2026 and never in production.

OpenRouter consumption: I used the provider's per-key figures. The account was created on 2026-08-22 at 22:06 UTC, so earlier months have no OpenRouter line. The explorer's day buckets are UTC: the first purchase was at 22:09:58 UTC, and the OpenCode sessions that consumed the 08-22 usage ran from 22:25 UTC. Sentinel is the key 'Sentinel evaluation', with $3.2630141728 of credits. The keys-page counter and two API key-counter checkpoints reproduce that figure. The balance is only consistent with it. The explorer CSV is $0.000749 lower because of rounding.

OpenRouter cost basis: credits were converted to cost by FIFO over the credit lots. All $4.2155 consumed to date fits in the first lot ($25 for $32.45, so 1.298 of cash per credit). That rate includes OpenRouter's 5.5% purchase fee and 23% Polish VAT, which is not reverse-charged because the invoice is addressed to a private person. Sentinel's economic cost is therefore $4.2353923963 in September 2026. In the cash table it is 13.05% of the 2026-08-22 payment. The 2026-09-23 payment gets 0%, because none of that lot is consumed. The $60.78 unspent balance is not a cost. This replaces the previous audit, which booked $3.2630 without VAT and kept a fee scenario ($0.1795) outside the totals; its '$3.44' figure was $3.2630 x 1.055.

TypeSafe: Sentinel's 162 jev-1.13.0 calls (2026-09-22/23) were re-derived from the union of the 9 cumulative usage.db copies (407 rows, so no row is counted twice). The token counts are provider-reported, and they are priced at the published $0.042 per million input tokens: $0.074125296. They were funded by the $5 promotional grant (owner statement), so the line is free_credit, zero cash and in_total=false. The TypeSafe console was not read. The previous audit's $0.0741 cost is therefore removed from the totals. The TypeSafe account was created on 2026-09-19, so there is no TypeSafe line before 2026-09.

Cross-group boundaries: every model called on the OpenRouter 'Sentinel evaluation' key is billed by OpenRouter. That covers the Anthropic models (Haiku 4.5 $2.668698, Sonnet 5 $0.056634), the OpenAI models (GPT-5.6 Luna, GPT-6 Luna, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Luna Pro, $0.433578 in the explorer, $0.43412162 per request) and Google Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite ($0.005368). The Anthropic, OpenAI and other groups must not add them. The verifier checked that the OpenAI portal-by-project figures for 2026-09-23 count a different set of requests, so there is no double count today. The Sonnet 5 calls here are Sentinel eval candidates on the Sentinel key; the rule that Sonnet 5 is msigalert applies to the Anthropic account, not to OpenRouter. The Luna rows in the Jev ledger ($0.10584204) belong to OpenAI. The OpenCode key ($0.952521) is excluded as a coding tool.

Totals for this group: the in-total economic cost is $4.2353923963 in 2026-09; 2026-08 and 2026-10 are $0 for both providers. Sentinel cash is $4.2353923963, inside the 2026-08-22 payment. The free-credit note line ($0.074125296) has zero cash and stays out of the totals. The run-rate is $0/month.

- NUMBERS 1 (the balance cannot settle the source choice): ACCEPTED. I reworded the ORT-2026-09 note. - ATTRIBUTION 4 (the failed_payment reason code): PARTLY ACCEPTED. The excluded-reason schema has no 'not_billed' or 'other' code, and 'failed_payment' misleads. So I removed the row from excluded and recorded the figure in the ORT-2026-09 notes. The figure is $0.245560855 of runner-retained reservations from the 4 smoke manifests (0.040061445 + 0.03706727 + 0.15728774 + 0.0111444); the verifier's 0.245560955 was a typo. run_rate.item: SCENARIO A: Twilio recharged under current routing (9-10 call + code SMS; 5-8 push-only) - incremental usage
run_rate.basis: estimate: urgency 9-10 alert events Oct 1-14 (15 events = 32.61 a month) x Jul 1-Aug 23 statement usage excluding rentals per urgency 9-10 event (USD 25.9845 / 47 events = USD 0.5529; calls unbilled, as on those statements)
run_rate.notes: Priced per alert event, not per logged attempt. Production alert records (events with urgency 9-10 that got a push record; server extract to 2026-10-14 15:37 UTC) give 47 such events in Jul 1-Aug 23 (75 accepted calls and 82 SMS, about 1.6 calls and 1.7 SMS per event, including re-call rounds when articles joined an unacknowledged event and update SMS), 33 in Sep 15-30, 15 in Oct 1-14 and 48 in Sep 15-Oct 14 (61 dispatch rounds, so 13 escalation updates). The journal's 290 call and 290 SMS attempts rejected in Sep 15-Oct 14 (58 + 58 in October) overstate demand: on the dead account the code SMS never arrives, so no event is ever acknowledged, and a rejected call leaves no alert record, so the retry-interval guard in _execute_phone_call (which looks at earlier call records) never holds a retry back. Sep 15 alone logged 96 rejected calls while 4 new urgency 9-10 events arrived. Central = 15 / 14 x 30.44 = 32.61 events a month x 0.5529 = 18.0312. Low = quietest rolling 7 days in October (Oct 6-12, 7 events) = 30.44 x 0.5529 = 16.8291. High = Sep 15-Oct 14 pace (48 / 30 x 30.44 = 48.70 events a month) with calls billed at June's rate (Jul 1-Aug 23 USD 25.9845 + 3.87 + 1.29 = 31.1445 / 47 = 0.6626 per event) = 32.2737. The busiest rolling week (Sep 23-29, 19 events) would run at about USD 54.75 a month while it lasts. Cross-check with the simpler pricing of one call (USD 0.0717 a minute) + one code SMS (July average USD 0.3072) + TTS per event and one update SMS per escalation: Sep 15-Oct 14 gives USD 22.5566 a month, inside the range. This replaces the earlier USD 14.6476 (Jul 1-Aug 23 average, about 26.5 events a month). Rentals (USD 5.15) are already in the lines above, so the full monthly cost after a recharge is about USD 23.18 (18.03 + 5.15), up to about USD 37.42 at the high bound. Reactivation first absorbs the debt: USD 9.4924 until 2026-10-20, USD 10.6424 from 2026-10-21, USD 14.6424 from 2026-10-28.

operational_risks: Since 2026-08-23 17:21 UTC the Twilio account is suspended for lack of funds and, as of 2026-10-14, left unfunded on purpose. No call or SMS has been accepted since 17:20 UTC that day. From 2026-09-01 02:55 UTC urgency-9 events got only a push, and the journal shows 290 call and 290 SMS attempts rejected (HTTP 401) between 2026-09-15 and 2026-10-14. These attempts came from 48 distinct urgency 9-10 events (61 dispatch rounds); the rest is retry inflation, because on the dead account no event is ever acknowledged and a rejected call leaves no record for the retry-interval guard. Urgency 9-10 phone calls are not being delivered.

A recharge first pays the debt before any call or SMS can go out: USD 9.4924 until 2026-10-20, USD 10.6424 from 2026-10-21 and USD 14.6424 from 2026-10-28. At scenario A pace (about USD 18.03 usage + 5.15 rentals = about USD 23.18 a month; about USD 37.42 at the high bound) a top-up of USD 50 on top of the debt lasts roughly 2 months (about 1.3 months at the high bound), less in an alert storm. Earlier suspensions ended when a manual top-up brought the balance positive.

Six earlier suspensions stopped all SMS and calls; each began 30 seconds to 3.5 minutes after the last accepted send, so Sentinel's own traffic emptied the balance. Outage windows (UTC): 2026-04-20 12:57 to 04-25 18:52 (about 5.2 days); 05-09 10:47 to 05-17 15:07 (about 8.2 days); 05-20 00:56 to 05-22 15:36 (about 2.6 days); 05-25 00:31 to 15:10 (about 15 hours); 05-29 02:42 to 18:01 (about 15 hours, which caused a missed urgency-9 call: five retries rejected 03:40-17:42); 06-02 18:11 to 06-03 11:14 (about 17 hours).

Auto-recharge (refill to about USD 20) worked from 2026-03-21 to 2026-04-10, then failed on 2026-04-17 (USD 10.23) and 2026-04-20 (USD 20.17) because the payment could not be processed. It is not configured now, so after any recharge the account will suspend again whenever the balance reaches zero; the only warning is the default low-balance email below USD 5.

Small manual top-ups lasted only days at pre-June volumes: USD 20 on 05-22 was gone by 05-25, and USD 20 on 05-25 by 05-29. Polish alert SMS are UCS-2 encoded (about 10.5 segments, roughly USD 0.48 per SMS), so SMS volume drains the balance fast.

The balance grows more negative by USD 5.15 a month with number renewals (US on the 21st, PL on the 28th). If Twilio eventually releases the numbers for non-payment, the Polish sender number may be lost and the sender configuration would have to change.
Only one card is on file now (a Visa); the two earlier cards are gone. A failed card payment stopped alerts in April.
